email.subject1: a signal play for Zus Health
email.body1:
Amy, saw Zus won the 2026 Interoperability Award and partnered with Elation to embed your aggregated patient profile into the EHR.

Wins and new partnerships usually mean more in-market healthcare accounts than the team can cover before the pipeline cools. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Zus off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Amy, quick follow-up for Zus.

Each new partnership usually pulls the number up faster than the headcount you can add to chase it. Most teams cannot say exactly how many meetings each rep needs to hit target, so the gap shows up late.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I will walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Zus needs to close that gap this quarter, plus where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Amy, last bit of proof for Zus.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and could not hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Zus's reply rate likely compares to other health-data platform teams. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?
email.body4:
Amy, I will stop reaching out on this one, but did not want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling enterprise pipeline without adding reps is not a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Standing up new EHR partnerships is its own kind of busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to your enterprise motion? I will tailor it to Zus either way.
